record.field: Create a new product, service or consumable in the catalogue

## When to use The user asks for a new product, service, subscription or consumable.
## Procedure 1. **Search first.** `search_records` on `product.template`, name `ilike` the product name. If something close exists, offer it instead of creating a duplicate. 2. **Queue a draft.** `create_draft` with `model: "product.template"` and `values: {"name": "<name>"}`. New products are ALWAYS `product.template` records — the variants (`product.product`) are created automatically by Odoo. Never queue a `product.product` without its template id. 3. **Send only what the user stated.** Name is the one field they gave. Everything else — price, cost, currency, category, uom, type — is Odoo's business. Odoo fills its own defaults.
## Where the values come from Three kinds of value, and only one of them is forbidden: - **Stated** by the user — use it. - **Found** by you this turn (a page you fetched, a record you read, a price you looked up) — use it. Looked up is NOT invented. If the user asked you to research, what you researched IS the answer they asked for; refusing to use it is refusing the job. - **Invented** by you — never. No price, SKU, reference, weight or spec that came from your own head.
So: no value without a source. A value you looked up has a source.
## Traps - **Never ask the user for a value Odoo already defaults.** Asking for price, currency or category when the user only said "iPhone 18 Pro" is a failure: create it with the name and let Odoo default the rest. - Never invent a SKU, barcode, internal reference or cost. Omit the field instead — a card with an invented value is worse than a card with a missing field. - **Do not stop to describe what you would do.** If the user asked for a change, the turn is not finished until the card is queued. A turn that ends with "I would now..." has done nothing. - **A product that already exists is an update, not a second product.** Find it, then set the fields on it — one card, several fields — instead of creating a duplicate. - `product.category` and `uom.uom` are the models for category and unit. There is no `product.uom`. - After the card is approved the template exists and its variant is usable; no second step is needed.
Bill a customer for delivered goods or services

## When to use The user wants to invoice a customer, bill a customer, or raise an invoice for work already done.
## Procedure 1. **Find the sale order** — `search_records` on `sale.order` for the customer and the unpaid lines. An invoice that already exists for those lines is a finding, not an obstacle: report it and stop. 2. **Check what is deliverable** — read the order's lines and their delivered state. Do not invoice what was never delivered without saying so. 3. **Invoice it** — `invoice_order` on the order id. It queues a card; the user approves. 4. **Report the number** — the invoice name and its total come from the card. Do not state a total you did not read from a tool.
## Traps - A customer invoice is `account.move` with `move_type = "out_invoice"`. A vendor bill is `in_invoice`. Always filter the type — an unfiltered search returns both and the answer is wrong. - One invoice per order, not one per line. `invoice_order` handles the grouping; do not queue one card per line. - `res.partner` has no customer flag. Filter `customer_rank > 0`. - Never invent a tax, a payment term or a journal. Omit the field.
Report which customer invoices are past due and by how much

## When to use The user asks who owes money, which invoices are late, or what to chase.
## Procedure 1. **Count first.** `count_records` on `account.move` with `move_type = "out_invoice"`, `payment_state` in `("not_paid", "partial")` and a due date in the past. The count is the headline of the answer. 2. **Then list them.** `search_records` with the same domain, ordered by due date ascending — the oldest debt first. 3. **Per row**: invoice number, customer, residual amount with its currency, and days overdue. 4. **One collection step.** Do not read every line of every invoice; the residual and the dates are on the header.
## Traps - Empty is a finding, not a failure: "no overdue invoices" is a complete answer. - Never round a residual to "0" without the count that says so. - `amount_residual` is the money left; `amount_total` is not. Reporting the total as the debt is wrong. - `payment_state` is the truth (`not_paid`, `partial`, `paid`); a date in the past alone does not mean overdue.
Record worked hours against a project task

## When to use The user says they worked on something, asks to log hours, or wants today's timesheet filled in.
## Procedure 1. **Find the task** — `search_records` on `project.task`, name `ilike` what the user said. If several match, ask with `ask_user` and 2-4 concrete options — never pick one. 2. **Log the hours** — `log_timesheet` with `task_id` and `hours`. A day is 8h, a morning is about 4h, and "an hour" is 1. If the user said nothing about duration, ask. 3. **The date** — "today" and "yesterday" are accepted words; pass "today" unless the user named another day.
## Traps - A timesheet is `account.analytic.line`. It needs a project and a task; the project is derived from the task. - Hours are a number between 0 and 24. "all day" is 8, not 24. - One card for the whole entry, not one per hour.
How to call read and write tools without failing

## Domains A domain is a **list of [field, operator, value] triples**, one list per condition:
``` [["name", "ilike", "Acme"]] [["move_type", "=", "out_invoice"], ["payment_state", "!=", "paid"]] ```
Never a flat triple, never a dict, never a bare string. Operators: `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, `like`, `ilike`, `in`, `not in`.
## Order of work 1. **Read first.** Search before you create — never create what might already exist. Then read the record, then act. 2. **One tool call per fact.** A search and a read of the same row are two facts, not one. 3. **Never guess an id.** No "id 1". Every id in a write must come from a tool result in this turn. A web page can never give you an Odoo id. 4. **Batch the reads.** Independent searches in one round beat three rounds of one.
## When a call fails Read the error, fix the argument, retry **once**. The same failing call twice is the failure. If the second attempt also fails, stop and use `inspect_method` (for a method's real parameters) or `fields_get` (for real field names) before trying again. If a field name is uncertain, ask the user.
## Writing - Only fields the user stated or a tool returned. Omit the rest. - A write always lands as a confirmation card. Saying "queued" without a tool call is a failure. - Chains: queue every step in dependency order in one turn and let the approvals fill the ids.
Ground every claim in a record and cite it

## When to use Any question about a record, a number, a list of records, or a decision. This is the default, not an option.
## Procedure 1. Every figure in the answer comes from a tool result in this turn. 2. Name the record it came from: the invoice number, the partner name, the project. A number without its source is a guess. 3. Read the record you cite. A citation to a record you did not read is worse than no citation.
## Shape - One line per finding, no paragraphs of preamble. - Say what is missing when something is missing: "no reorder points are on file, so the shortfall is computed as zero" is a finding. - A record you read can be cited with its deep link — the answer shows the record it came from and the user can open it.
## Traps - Never round to "zero" without the count that says so. - Never mix a total with a residual. - If a search comes back empty, say it is empty. Do not substitute a plausible-sounding number.
Read a scanned or PDF invoice into a draft vendor bill

## When to use The user attaches a bill, an invoice PDF or a scan and wants it in the books.
## Procedure 1. **Read the document** — `digitize_bill` on the attachment. It needs a model that can read images; a PDF with selectable text is better than a scan. 2. **Check for a duplicate** — search `account.move` for the vendor and the amount before queueing anything. 3. **Queue the bill** — a vendor bill is `account.move` with `move_type = "in_invoice"`, vendor, date, lines. 4. **Say what you could not read.** A scan that is half-legible gets a bill with the legible fields and a question about the rest — not a confident guess.
## Traps - A bill is `in_invoice`; an invoice you raise for a customer is `out_invoice`. Never queue the wrong one. - The amount on the document wins over anything inferred. - If the document is a scan the model cannot read, say so plainly instead of producing an empty bill.
Capture a durable fact or procedure worth keeping

## When to use The user taught you something that will matter next time: a naming convention, a business rule, a preference ("we always bill on the last day of the month"), a correction.
## Procedure 1. `write_knowledge` with a short `name`, a `description` that says **when this applies** (that line is what gets matched against a future request), and the `body` in markdown. 2. `kind`: `memory` for a fact about the business or the user, `wiki` for a concept, `skill` for a procedure to follow.
## Traps - It lands as a **draft**. A human reviews it before the agent may use it. Do not claim it is already in effect. - Never store a password, a key or a token. The tool refuses. - One concept per record. If it is two ideas, it is two records. - Do not propose what the tools already answer. A fact that a search returns is not knowledge.
